Create a production-ready TRANSPARENT pixel-art sprite atlas, using the attached island ONLY as style, lighting and camera-perspective reference. Do not draw the island. Exactly 4 columns × 4 rows = 16 equal square cells, chronological left to right, top to bottom. Each cell contains the SAME stationary complete furniture object: a compact warm oak academic workbench with four stout legs, a small blue laptop with cream keyboard, a brass compass on the tabletop and two slim books. 16 sequential frames: closed laptop, lid lifts over frames 1-4, screen powers on frames 5-6, tiny abstract career diagram changes frames 7-11, compass needle gently turns frames 12-15. No floating objects.
Critical: the furniture must look planted on the courtyard paving of the reference, not like a sticker/icon. Match its slightly elevated frontal/isometric perspective, warm sunlight from upper left, blue shadows, crisp deliberate pixel clusters, oak/cream/blue palette. Include a small subtle attached ground shadow in EACH cell. All four legs and all objects are visible. Exactly consistent object scale and camera in all 16 cells, the base/feet at 88% height in each cell, horizontal center 50%, body width 72% of cell. Keep at least 10% transparent margin on every side; no object crosses cells. Base and feet DO NOT move between frames; animate only the named item. Truly clear alpha outside sprites, NO colored matte, fog, sky, floor tile, text, letters, numbers, captions, grid or people. Image itself square. Detailed pixel illustration rather than smooth vector. No white outlines around sprite.
